### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

United States

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

ERROR: The extracted extension ('9') is unusual and will be skipped for safety reasons. If you believe this is an error, please report this issue on <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=> , filling out the appropriate issue template. Confirm you are on the latest version using yt-dlp -U

url: <https://www.pornhub.com/view_video.php?viewkey=68f88a68670d9>  
version: yt-dlp 2025.10.22

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

I need to remove the 'profiles' for it to work:

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Chile

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Apparently, since version 2026.01.29, not all audio tags 140 for the https protocol appear when the video has multiple audio tracks (however, all audio tracks for the m3u8 protocol do appear).

An example video that's live now and exhibiting this issue is (only the english track language for tag 140 of the https protocol is obtained): <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FkXhKu80CWU>

Previous versions of yt-dlp for this video link works ok and get all audio language tracks for the 140 https protocol

The verbose output for both versions is included below.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug/feature request

### Question

<https://archive.org/details/FOXNEWSW_20211112_060000_Tucker_Carlson_Tonight/start/0/end/60>

How do I download this full program? It seems to be broken up into 1-minute segments. In any case, simply issuing this url to yt-dlp yields nothing at all.

  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Right now I am attempting to download all videos in a two-week interval in November 2022 from a Rumble channel with 25,000 videos the last 3 years.

The routine way of doing this would of course be to issue the command (e.g.  
`yt-dlp -S res:360 --dateafter 20221106 --datebefore 20221115 https://rumble.com/c/RTNews`) and wait for yt-dlp to chug through the playlist, eventually sifting out the matching several hundred videos and downloading them.

This takes an inordinately long time.

The reason I use yt-dlp is that I am rarely online, so when I am connected I do a compressed process of downloading a huge amount of videos that I will watch until the next time I am able to connect and download more videos. So inordinate time consumption is not what I have time for.

The workaround for this that I have come up with for such very long playlists that are ordered chronologically is to wait for the perhaps 1000 pages of video urls to be grabbed by yt-dlp, and when that is done and the app begins to wade through the list of 25,000 videos to see which ones match my date interval criterion I break the Internet connection while yt-dlp is still working. This causes yt-dlp to slip through its 25,000 item list at a furious pace og perhaps 1,000 videos every 10 seconds.

I then watch the item counter increase until it gets somewhere near where I expect will be a date somewhat close to the desired time interval. So, when I see the counter reach 15,000 I reconnect to the Internet and find that I'm now in April 2023, i.e. only five months away from the wanted videos.

I can now let yt-dlp simply continue to run and finish the job, except this would still take a very long time- So I make a second disconnection and get to December 2022, Now I can easily let the regular process finish the job.

Except, sometimes the reconnection takes longer than expected, and we're now in September 2022.

So this is a hit and miss process. And if I miss I have to start from fresh having to wait first for yt-dlp to download 1,000 pages of video urls and then make a second attempt at slipping through the video counter and hopefully end up at a date that is conveniently close to the designated time interval but hasn't moved beyond it.

So even though it makes it possible for me to download playlist portions that I would otherwise not have time to sit around waiting for, it is cumbersome and very often frustrating, and quite often I fail to grab the videos from this particular playlist in the time I have before I have to go offline again.

WHAT I WANT

is a yt-dlp option for slipping to a particular number, e.g. `yt-dlp -sl 19000 playlist_url`.

I hope I have explained my wish comprehensibly.

To go with this feature I would like to be able to reuse the list of videos which yt-dlp first gets before starting to churn through the individual videos,

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

  * I'm reporting a broken site
  * I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2022.02.04**. ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are alive and playable in a browser
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl#video-url-contains-an-ampersand-and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)

Norway

### Description

<https://www.bitchute.com/playlist/wV9Imujxasw9/>

Unsupported url yt-dlp tells me.

(Verbose log shown with both the -v and -vU options below. The instructions here says to use -vU but that output looks less informative than the former.)

I also tried `yt-dlp --write-description --yes-playlist https://www.bitchute.com/video/yvvNqLcWePrk/?list=wV9Imujxasw9&randomize=false` going off the first video on the playlist, but only that one video got downloaded.

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood
    
    
              Not all data is extracted for all sites. Feel free to open a "site feature request"
    

_Originally posted by[@pukkandan](https://github.com/pukkandan) in [#4285 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4285#issuecomment-1515656262)_

Since the json file downloaded from Odysee when applying the `--write-comments` option doesn't in fact include the Comments section, I request that steps be taken to make sure this option works on Odysee videos!

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Attempting to download tracks from an unlisted (non-private) playlist on music.youtube.com.  
All tracks on the playlist are publicly available to all users on music.youtube.com.

  * For some tracks, yt-dlp extracts an unavailable URL for the track from the playlist which differs from the playable URL of the track, when the track is clicked into from the playlist and played individually
  * yt-dlp is able to download the track if the available URL for that track is provided, but cannot download the track from the playlist
  * yt-dlp can download other tracks from the playlist without issue 
    * No identifiable pattern for tracks which yt-dlp cannot download from the playlist vs ones that it can
  * For each track that cannot be downloaded, the error 'Video unavailable. This video is not available' is given, which indicates the video is not available on youtube.com, but the video is available on youtube.com
  * Track downloads without issue from youtube.com; issue is only present when downloaded from music.youtube.com



yt-dlp is extracting a URL to a version of the video that is unavailable, despite the video being available on youtube.com. I can't find a way to manually get to the same URL yt-dlp is getting - every version of the song I try to access has an available video, and downloads without issue if I provide the direct URL.

EXAMPLE:

  * URL for the track on music.youtube.com: 
    * <https://music.youtube.com/watch?v=vy2el0kqwLQ>
    * Downloads without issue
    * URL can be reached manually when track is clicked from the playlist on music.youtube.com
  * URL for the track on youtube.com: 
    * <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vy2el0kqwLQ>
    * Downloads without issue
    * URL can be reached manually when track is clicked from the playlist on youtube.com
  * URL for the video version of the track on music.youtube.com: 
    * <https://music.youtube.com/watch?v=UbQgXeY_zi4>
    * Downloads without issue
    * URL can be reached manually when video is clicked from the playlist on music.youtube.com
  * URL for the video version of the track on youtube.com: 
    * <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UbQgXeY_zi4>
    * Downloads without issue
    * URL can be reached manually when video is clicked from the playlist on youtube.com
  * URL yt-dlp extracts from the playlist on youtube.com: 
    * [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vy2el0kqwLQ&list=LL](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vy2el0kqwLQ&list=LL)
    * Downloads without issue
    * URL can be reached manually when track is clicked from the playlist on youtube.com
  * URL yt-dlp extracts from the playlist on music.youtube.com: 
    * <https://music.youtube.com/watch?v=L2Yog_3hvj4>
    * Unavailable, cannot be played or downloaded
    * URL cannot be reached manually



REQUEST: add support for music.youtube.com to download playlist tracks directly.

Current workaround: gather the correct URL for each track yt-dlp was unable to download from the playlist and download them individually.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/sergeychur)

[sergeychur](https://github.com/sergeychur)

opened [on Aug 21, 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10819#issue-2477780430)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Format 18 is broken for some videos on Youtube. Download for them hangs forever.  
For example youtube.com/watch?v=S7So-Kg81j4, youtube.com/watch?v=T82HxfZbQ7Y.  
If I cancel the download and relaunch, yt-dlp outputs `Did not get any data blocks`.  
Format is really broken, it timeouts after a second in browser too. But I believe it is not an expected behaviour for yt-dlp to hang forever instead of reporting an error and exit.

I've seen some similar issues concerning format 22 (downloading it also resulted in `Didn't get any data blocks`), but not with format 18 and not with infinite hanging.

It seems like issue happens here - 

[yt-dlp/yt_dlp/downloader/http.py](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/add96eb9f84cfffe85682bf2fb85135746994ee8/yt_dlp/downloader/http.py#L339)

Line 339 in [add96eb](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/add96eb9f84cfffe85682bf2fb85135746994ee8)

|  if not is_test and ctx.chunk_size and ctx.content_len is not None and byte_counter < ctx.content_len:   
---|---  
  
and here - 

[yt-dlp/yt_dlp/downloader/http.py](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/add96eb9f84cfffe85682bf2fb85135746994ee8/yt_dlp/downloader/http.py#L374)

Line 374 in [add96eb](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/add96eb9f84cfffe85682bf2fb85135746994ee8)

|  except NextFragment:   
---|---  
  
. For some reason yt-dlp thinks that receiving zero bytes is equivalent to NextFragment and doesn't increase retries counter. This results in infinite loop.

Fast workaround is to ban format 18 like format 22. But this can possibly happen with other formats (havn't seen it though).

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/xaocon)

[xaocon](https://github.com/xaocon)

opened [on Jun 30, 2023](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7472#issue-1782815517)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2023.06.22** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update)) or later (specify commit)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I tried to find any previous information about this but didn't see anything in READMEs, wiki, or in the `InfoExtractor` docstring. I looked some in the previous issues but there were thousands of results for not found and similar searches. I saw `_availability` but the options there don't seem to cover cases where the video doesn't exist for whatever reason.

It seems to be common to either raise `ExtractorError` or use `raise_no_formats()` with some kind of description about it. This seems like a common enough case to have documented standard and standard way to test for and report to user. I'm of the opinion that there should be a `class NotFoundError(ExtractorError):` or similar and that the `InfoExtractor` docstring should have a raises section but I don't know enough about the code base to know if that's really the right way to handle.

I'd be happy to try to help implement but wanted to have a discussion first.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Before submitting a _pull request_ make sure you have:

  * At least skimmed through [adding new extractor tutorial](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl#adding-support-for-a-new-site) and [youtube-dl coding conventions](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl#youtube-dl-coding-conventions) sections
  * [Searched](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/search?q=is%3Apr&type=Issues) the bugtracker for similar pull requests
  * Checked the code with [flake8](https://pypi.python.org/pypi/flake8)

### Description of your _pull request_ and other information

This supersedes [#682](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/682). (I'm making a new PR to keep things on topic - the other PR is a bit messy due to be experimental).

* * *

This PR adds support for falling back to the Innertube API when the webpage fails to download for whatever reason (429, network error, initial data extraction failure, etc.)

It is also possible to manually skip the webpage download by using `--extractor-args youtubetab:skip=webpage`

Also added a quick fix for the resolve MP to OLAK playlist handling, since that was broken.

At least at the time of writing, yt-dlp should now have a complete* workaround for the _common_ ** YouTube HTTP 429 error reported, for both video and tab extraction.  
*except private content accessible only through a secondary or greater account/channel  
**common referring to the webpage request getting 429nd only, but the API still works.

resolves [#926](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/926), resolves [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#23638](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/23638) (and most of the other 429 reports upstream)

**Known issues** :

  * When using cookies, the webpage is required to extract the required variables. Without this, the API requests will be for the first channel of the first account.

    * In the case of the user passing cookies, and the webpage failing to download, the tab extractor will raise an error. This is to stop unwanted behavior in variety of situations (e.g. an automated script to download a secondary channel liked playlist, but the webpage fails and starts downloading the first channel liked playlist).

    * Currently, the user can skip this check by passing `--extractor-args youtubetab:skip=authcheck`

  * channel search does not work (returns 0 results)

    * I think this is a YouTube a bug. YouTube appears to produce params for itself that it cannot understand.
    * See [[youtube:tab] Fallback to API when webpage fails to download #1122 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/1122#issuecomment-933214758)



**TODO:**

  * Improve the error message when authenticated but webpage fails.

  * ~~Fix unavailable video messages showing - test:<https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=UUTYLiWFZy8xtPwxFwX9rV7Q>~~ for another PR

Loading

###  Uh oh! 

There was an error while loading. [Please reload this page]().

Had to fix and improve the visitorData handling since the home/recommended was broken.

#### Some info on visitorData for the sake of documentation:

When YT gives `visitorData` in the `responseContext` of any API request, from what I see, is the most current one (so we need to update our `visitorData` to it). `visitorData` can change in some situations, such as [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#28702](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/28702). If YouTube doesn't provide `visitorData` in `responseContext`, `visitorData` is the same as before (i.e., does not need updating). We've seen it been used to keep track of what comment section version to use (ensure consistency) when YT was switching from the old to new API a while back. Along with the recommend feed and the playlists in the above issue, maybe this suggests it is some sort of token that identifies a session state?

* * *

After this PR I do need to go through YoutubeIE and clean up it's `visitorData` handling. I notice the comment one no longer works. Even though it may not be required as of now, it is good to have just in case (e.g A/B testing as mentioned before). Note: probably not a good idea to share visitorData across different clients.  
---

Loading

###  Uh oh! 

There was an error while loading. [Please reload this page]().

Some changes:

  * added a few tests for API Fallback mode
  * raise an error when url is not resolved (no `endpoint` provided) instead of unexpected tab not found error. This usually happens when, for example, an invalid playlist link is provided. Normally on YouTube it redirects to the home page.

Issue: channel search (e.g. <https://www.youtube.com/user/theCodyReeder/search?query=chicken>):

  * `resolve_url` endpoint resolves this correctly, but the `query` parameter that would usually be in plaintext json is instead in the protobuf `params`. YouTube's backend doesn't understand itself in this situation so the API fallback does not work in this case. 😆

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When running a yt-dlp command with `--simulate` (and without an `-f` arg), the default format selection differs from an unsimulated run under any of these conditions:

  * ffmpeg is not available
  * the outtmpl is `-`
  * the URL is for a livestream (and `--live-from-start` was not passed)



A dry-run/simulate option should actually simulate the behaviour that will occur when downloading.  
This behaviour is currently undocumented. Either the behaviour should be changed or at the very least be documented.

* * *

_Copying initial discussion:[#9805 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/9805#discussion_r1588171627)_

It looks like we can trace this logic back to [ytdl-org/youtube-dl@`0017d9a`](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/commit/0017d9ad6de831384e74db14a821e4c94020c9ac)

Back then, upstream's default format spec was only `best` if ffmpeg was not available. So a simulated run would result in a "requested formats not available" error if ffmpeg was not available and there was no combined video+audio format available. This `simulate` check seems to be added so that you could print json without having to manually pass `-f bv+ba` or `-f bv` etc in this scenario -- see the linked upstream PR

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

authored

Subtitle extraction from streaming media manifests [#247](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/247)

Authored by fstirlitz Modified from: [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#6144](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/pull/6144) Closes: [#73](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/73) Fixes: [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#6106](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/6106) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#14977](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/14977) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#21438](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/21438) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#23609](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/23609) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#28132](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/28132) Might also fix (untested): [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#15424](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/15424) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#18267](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/18267) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#23899](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/23899) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#24375](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/24375) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#24595](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/24595) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#27899](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/27899) Related: [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#22379](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/issues/22379) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#24517](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/pull/24517) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#24886](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/pull/24886) [ytdl-org/youtube-dl#27215](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/pull/27215) Notes: * The functions `extractor.common._extract_..._formats` are still kept for compatibility * Only some extractors have currently been moved to using `_extract_..._formats_and_subtitles` * Direct subtitle manifests (without a master) are not supported and are wrongly identified as containing video formats * AES support is untested * The fragmented TTML subtitles extracted from DASH/ISM are valid, but are unsupported by `ffmpeg` and most video players * Their XML fragments can be dumped using `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -f data -map 0 -c copy out.ttml`. Once the unnecessary headers are stripped out of this, it becomes a valid self-contained ttml file * The ttml subs downloaded from DASH manifests can also be directly opened with <<https://github.com/SubtitleEdit>> * Fragmented WebVTT files extracted from DASH/ISM are also unsupported by most tools * Unlike the ttml files, the XML fragments of these cannot be dumped using `ffmpeg` * The webtt subs extracted from DASH can be parsed by <<https://github.com/gpac/gpac>> * But validity of the those extracted from ISM are untested

## Description

[](https://github.com/leeblackc)

[leeblackc](https://github.com/leeblackc)

opened [on Apr 3, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12826#issue-2968998064)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

_No response_

### Example URLs

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OI4g4gElHG4>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Can we add an extra parameter in extractor-args to skip the v1/next request? If we only need to download the video and don't care about the extra data, this request is redundant.

[](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/21374847/429889723-74029237-26d2-4abf-811e-9a5fa5808bdf.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..oHQRepYoN40JoXW_svOUHMWXoueItEZyvzoEMoZXJ4c)

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
